AUTHOR: Allken
TITLE: A deep learning-based method to identify and count pelagic and mesopelagic fishes from trawl camera images
REGION: Norwegian Sea / Northeast Atlantic (IMR cruises May 2017 and 2018)
SPECIES: Blue whiting (Micromesistius poutassou), Atlantic herring (Clupea harengus), Atlantic mackerel (Scomber scombrus), mesopelagic fishes (Maurolicus muelleri + Benthosema glaciale grouped)
DATA: Public Deep Vision in-trawl image dataset (Allken et al. 2021, Geoscience Data Journal; NMDC) — D1 343 train images, D2/D3 1536 val/test images (D3 = 918 test); 20,000 synthetic images; ~2 million unannotated trawl images from 20 stations (2018)
V_EV: Discussion, Model limitations: 'Reasons for false positives (predictions > counts) include mis-identification due to poor lighting or partial fish (Figure 5c)'
D2: D1 343 train (+50% D2) / D2 val / D3 918 test; 82% of real images reserved for val/test
D_EV: Annotated datasets: 'The dataset D1 refers to the source-train2017-annotations.csv and source-train2018-annotations.csv in Allken et al. (2021), and D2 and D3 refers to the val_annotations.csv and test_annotations.csv'
R_EV: Results: 'Each trained model was then evaluated on the same test set, D3 of 918 images (Figure 1).' (same Deep Vision dataset, same cruises)
C_EV: Optimal score threshold: 'The maximum F1 score for all species together was obtained at a score threshold of 0.47 (Figure 2d).' ; 'the predicted count is inflated by multiple images taken of the same fish'
E_EV: Comparing image prediction counts and trawl catches: 'The prediction counts were compared with the trawl catches.' ; 'Overall catches and counts from images were correlated along a 1:1 linear regression in a log–log plot.'
ARCH: RetinaNet (Keras implementation, ImageNet-initialised, Adam lr 1e-5, 50 epochs) trained on real + synthetic (cut-and-paste) images; auxiliary CNN classifier to filter empty/krill images; linear (log-log) regression of counts vs catch
METR: mAP (IoU 0.5), per-class precision/recall/F1 vs score threshold, confusion matrix with missed detections and false positives, left/right camera count CV, regression of Deep Vision counts on trawl catch
NOTE: ENV coded NR because 'pelagic/mesopelagic open ocean (Norwegian Sea)' matches no allowed value. V: no turbidity/visibility metric; illumination (artificial lights, upgraded 2018, 'poor lighting' as error cause) and sampling depths (70-100 m, >250 m) are reported qualitatively (V2/V3 read as depth/illumination). D1: split follows the predefined csv splits of the authors' own published dataset (Allken et al. 2021); the paper does not state the split unit (image vs station), and both years/20 stations per year appear in train and test, so leakage across consecutive 200 ms frames is possible but not discussed (D4=N). R: all detection evaluation is on the same dataset; application to unannotated 2018 haul images is same cruise/camera, not external. C5: multi-frame duplicate counting is explicitly recognised and handled via species-specific count:catch ratios (10.4/15.4/40.0) and regression rather than tracking; FP/FN causes discussed in detail (Fig. 5); together with F1-derived threshold -> C_ALL=Y. E: counts compared with trawl catch per station (independent physical reference; mesopelagic fish absent from catch so not comparable) and with annotated test-set counts (895 vs 933 herring); FNR reported per species (E4=FNR). E3=없음: simple linear/log-log regression, not a hierarchical model. CODE=N: only the synthetic-image generation code is referenced via the data paper; FPS=Y refers to the 200 ms image interval.
